note: All original 33 top-level modules remain accounted for. Target depth is a plan, not implementation evidence. Status vocabulary: IMPLEMENTED_SANDBOX_SUBSET means the named behaviour is built and exercised in the customer-local synthetic profile, never that the master module is delivered; PARTIAL_SANDBOX means only the stated part exists; NOT_IMPLEMENTED means nothing is built. COVERED_AT_CANDIDATE means executing suites covered the behaviour at the frozen candidate and is engineering evidence only. It is not canonical acceptance, which requires APPLICATION_ACCEPTANCE and FULL_SCENARIO records from the two human rehearsals; every canonical test T01-T34 remains NOT_RUN. Evidence names the suites and browser specs that cover the module. The exact executed artefacts for the frozen candidate are listed in artifacts/release-manifest.json under exact_candidate_evidence.

capabilities.name: Identity and Access Management
capabilities.limitation: Real library-backed staff and principal sessions, scoped roles, privileged MFA and server-side capability checks against OPA. No enterprise SSO, SCIM or directory federation.

capabilities.name: Tenant Management
capabilities.limitation: Tenant, legal entity and environment scoping enforced by explicit predicates and row-level security, proven by cross-tenant and sibling-environment denial. Two synthetic organisations only; no tenant lifecycle administration.

capabilities.name: Privacy Control Graph
capabilities.limitation: Relational inventory over PostgreSQL: data assets with parent/child structure, reviewed category assignments, processing activities, typed foreign-key-backed relationships, distinct ASSERTED/OBSERVED provenance with freshness bounds, bounded keyword search, bounded traversal to depth three, change impact over policies, workflows, tests, assets and owners, and justified payload erasure that preserves historical links. Not an autonomous estate discovery scan and not a graph database. Impact does not cover assessments, processor relationships or retention plans, which are not implemented in this release and are reported as explicitly unavailable rather than empty.

capabilities.name: Policy Engine
capabilities.limitation: Separate administrative and processing policy namespaces in OPA, immutable published policy versions, distinct-reviewer re-authentication, and a preview that is explicitly not an admission decision. Fixed condition forms, not arbitrary policy authoring. Fails closed on policy outage.

capabilities.name: Workflow Engine
capabilities.limitation: Transactional outbox, durable Temporal worker and bounded retry and reconciliation, surviving worker and application restart. One withdrawal workflow family; no workflow designer.

capabilities.name: Connector Framework
capabilities.limitation: Locally signed, scope-bound agent commands against three declared connector kinds: synthetic CRM, local REST simulator and an explicitly unsupported legacy target. Synthetic targets only; no real vendor connectors.

capabilities.name: Verification Engine
capabilities.limitation: Independent scoped reads recording method, observed target generation, freshness and scope, kept separate from execution receipts, with explicit EFFECT_UNKNOWN and read-based reconciliation. An acknowledgement is never treated as verification.

capabilities.name: Evidence Engine
capabilities.limitation: Persisted receipt, action and observation timeline with authenticated JSON export carrying an integrity digest and explicit coverage limits, including unresolved obligations. Local evidence only; the digest detects change against a trusted reference and does not prove external effects. §133 asks for evidence export as JSON, CSV where appropriate, PDF reports and signed evidence packages, and says the exports themselves must be audited. The JSON export above was the only one built; printable reports are now built too. A report is a period, a scope and an ordered selection of ten sections, each a table assembled from records this installation already keeps rather than figures this path computes for itself -- a report that derived its own numbers would be a second source of truth able to disagree with the screens. Generating one is an ordinary audited read, so §133's requirement that exports be audited is met by the same mechanism every other route uses, and the integration suite checks the event is there. Four presets exist for the shapes an organisation actually asks for -- full record, board pack, response to a regulator or auditor, internal control review -- and each is only an ordered selection of the same sections, so a preset can show nothing a manual selection could not. Two refusals protect the person who is handed the report rather than the person who made it, because they did not assemble it and cannot see what is missing: every section this installation could have produced and did not is named on the cover with whether it was not selected or withheld, and a section the generator lacks the authority to read is named as withheld rather than dropped -- an ORG_ADMIN may export evidence but deliberately not the audit trail, and their report says so instead of quietly shrinking to fit them. Nothing here grades, scores or certifies, and the contract refuses any such field. CSV export is built. A section is already a header row and data rows of plain strings, which is exactly where §133's "CSV where appropriate" applies, and a section or the whole report downloads as one file per section. It is produced from the validated, digested report the server already returned rather than from a second query, for the same reason the print layout is: a CSV derived independently would be a second source of truth able to disagree with the report. Every field is quoted and embedded quotes doubled, so a value containing a comma, a newline or a leading equals sign cannot shift columns or be read as a spreadsheet formula, and a byte-order mark is written so the Eighth Schedule languages open correctly. The report digest is in every filename, because a CSV carries the table and nothing else -- the period, the scope, the sections left out and each section's caveats live in the report, so a spreadsheet on its own is deliberately not the record. What is still not built from §133: signed evidence packages. The installation does hold an Ed25519 key, but it is the key that signs commands to the agent, and reusing it for evidence provenance would conflate two trust domains -- a party able to verify an evidence package would be verifying with the same identity that authorises action on customer systems. A separate evidence-signing key is a key-custody decision under §172 and is not taken here. No PDF is generated server-side either -- the report is laid out for paper with print rules and the operator saves it as PDF from the browser, which keeps the delivered lockfile unchanged and avoids this product promising that a binary it rendered faithfully represents the records behind it.

capabilities.name: Privacy Test Engine
capabilities.limitation: Executable regression scenarios with real assertions: a healthy run passes, a deliberately broken control is detected and keeps its real FAIL, a repaired run passes, and an interrupted run is recovered as ERROR with no fabricated pass. Read by exact run identifier; no run-history list.

capabilities.name: Notification Engine
capabilities.limitation: Versioned templates with content digests and a stated purpose; notification tasks raised only against a record that exists (coverage gap, notification obligation or assessment finding); and an append-only delivery log in which queued, sent, delivered, failed and acknowledged are five independent facts that keep their real order. Only queueing is performed by ORVIA and needs no evidence; every later fact is a recorded claim that must name evidence, and a channel with no configured transport is declared unavailable and cannot be claimed as sent. A failure and a later success are both retained. Escalation raises attention on overdue undelivered tasks and never moves the deadline that caused it, enforced by a database trigger and by a literal-zero field in the sweep result. Not included: any actual transport (no mail, no webhook egress, no in-app inbox delivery), recipient preference rules, per-principal notification, scheduled sweeps (escalation runs on demand) and vendor billing notifications.

capabilities.name: Consent Management
capabilities.limitation: Affirmative purpose-specific grant against an exact notice version, monotonically increasing epoch, immutable receipt, withdrawal that never requires accepting a new notice, and replay and freshness safety at consumption.

capabilities.name: Notice Management
capabilities.limitation: Immutable published notice versions with content digest and publication time, referenced by exact version at the moment of consent. A notice may be authored in English or any of the twenty-two Eighth Schedule languages, which is the set Act s5 permits; the closed list is enforced by the contract and again by a database check, and the language column is generated from the notice document so the two cannot drift apart. A data principal records the language they chose, and only the principal may set it. The language asked for and the language served are separate fields everywhere they appear: where this installation has no notice in the chosen language it serves English and reports the request as unmet, which the schema makes the only expressible answer -- reporting a fallback as though the choice had been honoured is refused at parse time. A change to a notice is classified as editorial, a translation or a material change to scope. An editorial fix or a translation cannot carry a consent decision because nothing material changed; a material change cannot be recorded without one; and a translation must name the version it translates and be in a different language from it. The number of grants affected is counted from the consent records at the moment of the decision and the record says so structurally, so the figure can never be asserted. Every classification is append-only and one per version. Previously recorded as fully implemented while FR-M12-03 and FR-M12-04 had no code at all; that was wrong and is corrected here. Not included: this product does not translate, so a notice in a language is one somebody authored in it; there is no translation-staleness detector beyond the recorded source version; requiring fresh consent records the decision and does not itself withdraw anything; notice delivery management is still absent; and the workspace has no screen for classifying a change, so FR-M12-03 is API-only. Rules 3 and 9 require itemised notice content and appropriate contact information, and the master's own list of what the notice system must support names Data categories. A notice now carries both as structured facts rather than prose: the personal data it covers is itemised from the same closed vocabulary the inventory uses, so what a notice claims and what the inventory records can be compared instead of being two independent descriptions, and a notice cannot be created that itemises nothing or names the same item twice. Act §5(1)(b) and (c) are three separate channels rather than one contact string -- how to exercise rights including withdrawal, how to raise a grievance, and how to complain to the Data Protection Board -- because they routinely have different destinations and a single field would hide an omitted one. The data principal sees the itemisation in their own portal, which is where §5(1) matters. What this deliberately does not do is judge whether a notice is legally adequate: there is no field in which a notice could be marked compliant, lawful or certified, and the check is that the items exist rather than that they are sufficient. The 324 notices that already existed when this was introduced report that their itemisation was never recorded rather than being back-filled: inventing the items of a notice somebody has already been shown and consented to would misrepresent what they agreed to, and a structural companion field makes an un-itemised notice impossible to read as one that itemises an empty list. This was a non-additive contract change, so the executable transport moved to 0.15.0.

capabilities.name: Data Principal Portal
capabilities.limitation: Separate data principal authentication domain and portal showing own choices, notice, receipts and history, with grant and withdrawal. A principal cannot reach the workspace and sees no other principal, staff identifier or workflow internal.

capabilities.name: Rights Management
capabilities.limitation: Rights request lifecycle using the master state vocabulary and its exact transition map, with identity, authority, execution, response and scope held as five independent dimensions. Identity match grading (exact/strong/probable/ambiguous/no-match) blocks disclosure and destructive execution while unresolved. Nomination and guardian mandates are separate authorities with permitted-right scope, validity windows and revocation that immediately withdraws authority from open requests. Execution is computed only from recorded per-system outcomes, never from a lifecycle transition: success must name its method and evidence, an unsupported connector operation cannot be claimed, and a system with a recorded outcome cannot be dropped or re-actioned by re-scoping. CLOSED is administrative closure that cannot rewrite what execution achieved. Portal self-service intake is built. The Act gives these rights to the data principal, so a product where only staff could raise a request made the organisation the gatekeeper of a right it does not own; recording somebody else's request for them is a fallback, not the mechanism. A principal now raises their own request from the privacy portal, and three things are structural rather than procedural. The principal is taken from the authenticated session and never from the body, so there is no field through which one person could raise a request about another -- the contract refuses principal_id, on_behalf_of, subject_id and mandate_id on a portal request, and the database refuses the row as well through app.own_principal. The channel is not the caller's to choose: a row inserted from the portal says PORTAL, because that field is what later tells an auditor how the request actually arrived. And identity is recorded from the authentication that already happened rather than re-graded by a human -- the session binds exactly one principal reference, which is an exact match to one reference as a matter of fact, and asking an operator to review it would replace a fact with an opinion. The principal's own policies are SELECT and INSERT only: a requester can never update or delete a request, because how it moves is the organisation's act and a requester able to edit the record could rewrite what they had asked for. What the requester sees is deliberately narrower than the staff record -- no identity grading, no per-system planned actions, no unresolved destinations -- because those describe how the organisation is built and what it could not reach, which the requester cannot act on. Closed and answered stay separate facts, and the portal says plainly that a state is where a request has got to rather than a promise about the outcome. Still not included: automatic dispatch of planned actions through the durable workflow engine (outcomes are recorded by an operator or an external process, not driven by ORVIA), age assurance, and response package generation beyond the reviewed release record.

capabilities.name: Retention Management
capabilities.limitation: Retention evaluated per copy against the M03 inventory, with reviewed constraints (trigger, basis, source reference, minimum/maximum, permitted use, owner, review and release condition), exact-scope legal holds that name the copies they cover, and reviewed conflict decisions. Three refusals are enforced end to end: a copy with no recorded basis is never eligible for deletion; constraints that disagree block until a reviewer records which governs, rather than applying the longest duration; and a backup copy can never be reported as suppressed or deleted because backup erasure is not independently verifiable. Outcomes are recorded per copy class and are append-only. Not included: execution through connector adapters (outcomes are attested, not dispatched), crypto-shredding, backup-expiry tracking, and automatic reconciliation of a quarantined restore, which is surfaced as a blocker for an operator to clear.

capabilities.name: Processor/Vendor Management
capabilities.limitation: Processor relationships with authorised purposes and categories, region, contract reference, owner and incident contact; declared processor-to-system links; assessments activated by a reviewed applicability basis; and findings with owner, severity and deadline. The defining rule is enforced at every layer: notification, acknowledgement and verification are three separate append-only facts, only an independent check with named evidence can record verification, and a processor statement is always an attributable claim. Standing reports the three facts separately with no combined score, and derives systems serving purposes the processor was never authorised for. An assessment cannot complete while its findings are open, and a finding closes only with defined evidence or a retest. Not included: any automated exchange with a processor (every fact is recorded locally by a person), SDF or sector-specific rule packs beyond the assessment kind, sub-processor chain discovery, and contract document storage.

capabilities.name: Privacy Incident Explorer
capabilities.limitation: Incidents recording occurrence, detection and awareness as three separate moments whose real ordering is enforced at the boundary and in the database, with unknown kept as unknown rather than filled in from another moment. Notification obligations are computed per recipient from rule packs the customer recorded and activated: ORVIA ships no notification periods, and each rule names its own reviewed source, the moment its clock runs from and how long it allows. A duty whose clock has not started has no deadline rather than a guessed one, and a rule that does not apply while the affected scope is uncertain is recorded as not applicable rather than skipped. Corrections append with their previous value and name every deadline they moved. A dispatch is a recorded claim that must name evidence, a dispatched notification cannot be withdrawn, and where no supported channel exists a manual package is required. Not included: any actual filing or message transport (ORVIA sends nothing), regulator API integration, notification content drafting, and scheduled escalation of overdue duties, which are visible but trigger no alert.

capabilities.name: Coverage and Failure Center
capabilities.limitation: Coverage computed at read time over the recorded inventory across five dimensions, each reporting its own numerator, denominator and explained exclusions. Attention states are reported as overlapping sets that name what they overlap with and are never summed into a headline figure. Gaps are derived from real rows (missing retention basis, never observed, stale observation, unreviewed inventory, unresolved destination, failed execution), refreshed rather than duplicated on re-derivation, keep their original detection date, and close only through named evidence or an owned and reasoned acceptance of risk; a recurrence opens a new gap. Runbook guidance is advisory only and cannot establish a cause, close an action or produce a decision. Not included: coverage over systems nobody declared, scheduled derivation, notification of overdue gaps, and connector-capability change detection as a gap source.

capabilities.name: AI Privacy Copilot
capabilities.limitation: No learned model/runtime/import workbench in this sprint

capabilities.name: AI Discovery
capabilities.limitation: Retained custom-model future function

capabilities.name: AI Policy Builder
capabilities.limitation: Retained custom-model future function

capabilities.name: AI Workflow Builder
capabilities.limitation: Retained custom-model future function

capabilities.name: AI Risk/Drift Analysis
capabilities.limitation: Retained custom-model future function; deterministic regression remains V1

capabilities.name: AI Test Generation
capabilities.limitation: No generation needed for deterministic test engine

capabilities.name: AI Incident Analysis
capabilities.limitation: Retained custom-model future function

capabilities.name: Billing
capabilities.limitation: Out of sprint scope. No billing, metering, invoicing or payment capability exists.

capabilities.name: Licensing
capabilities.limitation: Immutable signed licences carrying only edition, entitlements, validity, licensed limits and an installation binding. The claims schema is closed, so a licence cannot carry a command, an endpoint or an authority grant, and the entitlement vocabulary cannot express a capability this product will not sell. Local verification covers trusted signer, audience, signature over canonical JSON, schema, installation binding and validity window, and every failure returns a named reason. Re-importing the same licence is refused as a replay; a stored licence can be superseded but its terms and validity cannot be edited and it is never deleted. Not included: offline renewal flows, revocation lists and freshness policy, trusted-time handling beyond the local clock, and any vendor-side issuance. The signing key is supplied by configuration with no default: without it nothing verifies.

capabilities.name: Entitlements
capabilities.limitation: Five independent gates — release availability, deployment support, controlled rollout, licence entitlement and actor authorisation — every one of which must pass before a feature is usable, each reported separately with its own reason so the blocking gate is identifiable. One shared capability vocabulary rather than scattered price checks. Expiry restricts new work and never removes recorded evidence or the ability to read and export. Capabilities that no edition, licence or flag can enable (model features, vendor remote access, staff directory sync, proactive diagnostics, runtime replication) are stated to the operator as commitments rather than withheld features. On licensed limits, the earlier wording here was misleading and is corrected: it read as an unfinished feature when there is in fact no operation to enforce against. Environments and staff members are created only by the protected local bootstrap in scripts/auth-bootstrap.ts; this build exposes no API route that creates either, so the recorded environment and staff limits cannot be exceeded through the product. That comparison is now made and reported: the entitlement report carries each licensed limit beside the count this installation actually holds, with whether it is within the limit derived from the two figures rather than stated separately, so a report cannot claim to be inside a limit it is over. Environments are counted for the organisation and staff from the scoped identity summary, because the application role cannot read the identity store directly. A structural field says the limit is reported and never enforced here, which is the honest verb when the product creates neither resource. With no licence imported the comparison is empty rather than passing, because there is nothing to compare against and that is a different fact from being within every limit. Also not included: downgrade hand-off workflows, and edition-differentiated behaviour beyond entitlement membership.

capabilities.name: Customer Onboarding
capabilities.limitation: FR-M29-01, FR-M29-02 and FR-M29-03 are built; FR-M29-04 is not, which is why this stays partial. A protected local bootstrap provisions one organisation and a unique generated owner credential and initialises the profile, roles and synthetic fixtures; it remains command line only. Eleven preflight gates answer the checks the master requires before go-live, each by examining something rather than asserting it: the address this process is actually serving on, the Node version and architecture it is executing on, the scheme it serves and whether that address is reachable off the host, the database's own fsync and synchronous_commit settings, the count of active primary owners in this organisation's local identity store read through a view that exposes two integers and nothing else, the signing key identifiers present in the running environment, the configured connection endpoints outside loopback, the telemetry switches of every third-party component, the licence validity window, and whether the installed version has a signed release manifest behind it. Ten of the eleven are genuinely checkable here. The backup target is not, and it reports NOT_VERIFIABLE_HERE with the reason rather than a comfortable pass; it is listed separately from the failing gates and the report states structurally that an unverified gate is not a passed gate. There is no overall verdict, no score and no percentage, and no field through which eleven technical checks could be restated as readiness or compliance. Each gate carries the sentence naming exactly what it examined, because several are narrower than their names suggest -- the egress gate reads the configuration, not the host firewall, and says so. The nine-step guided connection runs in the customer workspace. A step is never a tick: four steps record a decision the customer made and five are answered by reading evidence kept elsewhere (a capability check, an approved resource, a target mapping, a preview decision), so a step stops being done when its evidence is withdrawn. A connection cannot be started asking for a right to change the connected system, production scope is stated rather than inferred, what was requested and what was observed are separate fields, and an unchecked system reports both observations as unknown rather than denied. The connection secret is never held here, only a reference behind a pattern that refuses whitespace and anything long enough to be a pasted credential. Enablement is a three-rung ladder that only climbs; approved enforcement is refused for a system no recorded check found able to restrict, in the application and again in a trigger, and enabling is a separate capability from configuring. Three workspace screens read this: the preflight gates, the connection list and a per-connection step view. FR-M29-04 is built as one typed path, which is exactly what OPEN-11 permits: implement one approved typed path fully before writing another parser, and no arbitrary upload-to-table tool. That path is a data-asset inventory. There is one import kind in the contract, the declared row shape is the parser so there is no looser parsing step behind it, and there is no field anywhere through which a file, a blob, a delimiter or a target table name could arrive. Rows land in quarantine as the only entry state; the preview names, per row, whether it collides with nothing, restates something already recorded, or disagrees with an existing asset and which one; a disagreement blocks the apply until a named person decides to skip it or import it separately; and conflicts are recomputed at apply rather than trusted from the preview, because the inventory can change in between. Purge really deletes the quarantined rows and keeps the batch record saying it was purged, when and why, so a purge never becomes indistinguishable from an import that was never submitted -- the database refuses to delete the batch. The requirement's last clause is the one that shapes the rest: everything applied is written with provenance ASSERTED and review state UNREVIEWED through the ordinary creation path, and the graph schema already refuses to let an ASSERTED record carry an observation time or freshness window, so an import cannot manufacture an observation even by trying. A source snapshot is never presented as evidence that any control is in force, and two structural literals say so. What is narrow and stated: one import kind, a 500-row ceiling per batch, and collision detection on name within a system rather than on any richer row identity -- the row-identity and atomic-versus-partial semantics OPEN-11 leaves open are not pre-empted here. Also absent: there is no wizard for the earlier organisation, industry, admin and deployment steps; the customer-held recovery route FR-M29-02 names is not built, only the single primary owner it also names; connectivity and certificate verification are recorded as the customer performed them rather than observed by this product; the preflight report reads the installation at one moment and does not watch it; and a connection's scope is narrowed by withdrawing approved resources, not by deleting the connection, which is kept.

capabilities.name: Support Bundle System
capabilities.limitation: Local support cases linked to a coverage gap, fixed-schema diagnostic generation, digest-bound approval, operator-recorded transfer, canary registration and a local copy of the vendor ingress validator. Minimisation is structural rather than procedural: every field of a diagnostic report is an enum, integer, timestamp, version or digest, so a log line, an operational summary or a principal reference has no field to occupy, and the installation is named only by a one-way digest. An approval names the exact payload digest that was previewed and carries no authority to generate; a regenerated report supersedes the previous draft, so an approval cannot travel to it. The ingress validation table has six columns beyond scope and none of them can hold a body, so a rejected submission is not retained. The vendor case state and the local control state are two separate facts: the local state is read from the linked coverage gap on every request and a vendor closing their case leaves it exactly where it was. Absent by design and not merely unbuilt: there is no support transport at all, so a recorded transfer is an operator attestation rather than an observed delivery, and nothing here sends, uploads or receives anything. Two workspace screens read this: support cases, which show the vendor case state and the local control state as two columns that are never combined, and the registered canaries, which show digests and never the tokens themselves. Generating a draft, approving one and recording a transfer are now available from the screen rather than the API alone, so an operator can actually run the flow. Each control is deliberately narrow: generating produces and stores a report and cannot approve or carry anything; approval submits the previewed payload digest rather than a typed one, and refuses outright on a superseded draft, so an approval always names a payload the approver saw; and recording a transfer is worded throughout as an operator attestation, because this product has no support transport and neither sent the payload nor observed it arrive. Still not included: canary registration remains API-only; retention is not enforced against the recorded approval window; and a canary cannot be withdrawn once registered.

capabilities.name: Updates
capabilities.limitation: Immutable signed release manifests carrying provenance, a dependency inventory, per-migration notes and the supported profile list; eight separately named eligibility checks reported individually and stated not to be permission to execute; a recovery mode derived from the declared migrations rather than chosen; and an append-only migration ledger. Trust is re-evaluated at eligibility rather than inherited from import, so a manifest signed by a key this installation no longer trusts becomes ineligible. One irreversible migration forces forward recovery and the schema refuses to express a rollback claim alongside it. An update is recorded as applied only when all seven steps have succeeded, including boundary revalidation and core regression, and the database refuses the applied state otherwise, so an interrupted run stays visibly interrupted. Absent, and this is the main limit: no artifact is fetched, unpacked or executed. Archive safety and expansion ratio are decided from the signed manifest before anything would be written, but this module records and gates an update a customer performs; it does not perform one. Three workspace screens read this: imported releases with their eligibility reported check by check, update plans with everything still outstanding and both post-change facts shown separately, and the installed version history. The plan list exists because without it an interrupted update was reachable by nobody. Approving a plan and recording a step are now available from the screen. Approval requires the recovery mode to be acknowledged explicitly rather than defaulted, because a release carrying an irreversible migration fixes the recovery mode for the whole update and an operator who missed that has no way back; and the evidence field for a step appears exactly when the step is claimed to have succeeded, which is the claim the contract refuses without evidence. Both are worded as recording what a person did: this product fetches, unpacks and runs nothing. Still not included: release import is API-only; rollback is never executed for a reversible release; and the release signing key has no default — without ORVIA_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY and ORVIA_RELEASE_KEY_ID nothing imports.

capabilities.name: Monitoring
capabilities.limitation: FR-M32-01, FR-M32-02 and FR-M32-03 are built and qualified. Liveness, dependency readiness and business readiness are three separate verdicts with three separate reasons and there is no field that combines them, because the failure worth catching is an installation that answers every probe while being unable to carry out a single privacy decision — the integration suite drives exactly that state and asserts that only the third verdict moves. Seven operational signals are reported: worst propagation delay, oldest unresolved work, observation freshness, undispatched queue depth, database size and backup status are measured from this installation's own tables; connector limit headroom reports that it was not measured and why, because this build has no measured connector load budget. An unmeasured signal and a signal measured at zero never share a representation, and backup status reverts to unmeasured — never to zero — where no snapshot has been declared. Everything collected is a count or a duration, so the minimisation is a property of what is selected rather than a promise about redaction. FR-M32-03 is deliberately not a backup tool: ORVIA does not create, encrypt, store, move or read an archive, and two structural fields on every snapshot say so and cannot be flipped. What is built is the part only this product can do — a digested statement of what this installation saw when a snapshot was declared, and a refusal to let a restore resume until every consent decision that changed since the snapshot has been decided by a named person, with release held behind its own capability so the person who ran the restore is not automatically the person who signs it off. Deciding that the current state prevails leaves the withdrawal standing, and the integration suite asserts that the person who withdrew is still withdrawn after the restore is released. This is the OPEN-09 interim rule (quarantine when current state cannot be established; no reconstructing new events from an old backup) and not a resolution of OPEN-09: no store topology, backup boundary or measured loss/recovery window is chosen or claimed, and this build makes no RPO or RTO statement. FR-M32-04 is built as far as this deployment permits, and the part that is not is stated rather than simulated. There is no vendor-side application in V1 and no vendor service anywhere in this build, so there is no vendor console to render and vendor service health is reported as unobserved with the reason — never as healthy. What is built is the customer-side account of the restriction the requirement imposes: every payload that has ever left this installation towards the vendor, derived from records already kept, each approved by a named person against one exact digest and each recorded as carried by a person rather than sent by the product. The report distinguishes approved-and-carried from approved-and-never-carried, counts cases that disclosed nothing so an open case is never read as a transfer, and states structurally that it describes what was disclosed and not what the vendor holds, which this product cannot see. The three prohibitions are enforced rather than asserted: no automatic channel exists for anything to travel on, the disclosed facts are closed diagnostic codes with occurrence counts and windows and none of them can name a person, and the unit suite checks the diagnostic, support-subject, incident-severity and incident-state vocabularies contain no term by which a model-absence incident could be written, so adding one fails the suite. M32 therefore stays PARTIAL_SANDBOX: the vendor-side surface itself is absent because there is nothing to host it, and that absence is not something the customer-side report makes up for. Also present from earlier work: local service preflight, an unauthenticated liveness endpoint, and a correlation identifier on every audited request. No metrics series, alerting, tracing or uptime history is retained — nothing here is stored or sent anywhere.

capabilities.name: Audit Administration
capabilities.limitation: FR-M33-01 and FR-M33-03 are built; FR-M33-04 is not, which is why this stays partial. A coverage report answers the eight named categories from the trail itself rather than from a list somebody maintained, so a category cannot be reported as covered because a setting said so, and the two categories this build has no route for say that instead of reading as an auditing gap -- 'nothing has happened' and 'nothing here can happen' never share a shape. The trail is readable scoped to one organisation, filtered only by five declared keys that reach the database as bound parameters, and paginated by id. Reading it is itself an audited event, so a quiet look leaves a trace. Reading, exporting and administering are three separate permissions: an organisation administrator may read the trail but not take it out of the installation, an auditor may do both but may not dispute a record, and only the owner may append a correction. An export carries every event its filter matched or it is refused by name -- there is no partial export, and the digest covers exactly the events carried. Correction is by appending: a dispute names the event, states which of five reasons applies and what the recorder believes, and the original is untouched; PostgreSQL triggers refuse every UPDATE and DELETE on both the trail and the corrections, so a role that bypasses row-level security cannot shorten either. Two workspace screens read this: audit coverage and the audit trail, the latter offering an export of exactly what is displayed. FR-M33-04 is built. Each of the eight audited categories is retained under exactly one of four stated purposes, which the contract enforces so no part of the trail is kept for a reason nobody gave. No retention period ships: OPEN-10 forbids universal statutory retention numbers, so a purpose with none configured reports that rather than defaulting to a number or to forever, and recording one is refused unless it names what the period rests on. Rules are superseded rather than edited and the database refuses an UPDATE or DELETE even from the migrator, because shortening a period is exactly the change somebody would make to clear a backlog. Payload minimisation is measured rather than promised: app.audit_events has no payload column and never had one, the report counts payload-shaped columns at read time, and the contract permits only zero -- so adding such a column stops the report rendering instead of letting it keep describing an envelope-only trail. For the same reason there is no justified payload deletion for a truthful envelope history to survive; the envelope is the whole record and 0027's trigger preserves it absolutely. Retention is therefore a schedule and a disclosure, never a purge: an elapsed period is reported and the integration suite proves reading the schedule deletes nothing and that the database still refuses to remove an overdue event. Tested backup handling is the honest half: the report counts declared snapshots covering the trail and states that nothing it describes reaches a copy inside one, because the archive is the customer's and outside this product. What would still need deciding before audit envelopes could be deleted at all is the record-class question OPEN-10 leaves open, and this build does not pre-empt it. FR-M33-02 is met by there being no vendor-facing audit surface at all rather than by a separation this module built. Also absent: a correction cannot be withdrawn once appended, the export ceiling is a fixed count rather than a streamed file, and the screens report and correct but do not schedule anything.
